findings.description: Calling stats.clear() on the shared per-decorator statistics dict, instead of binding a fresh dict, wipes the statistics of any in-progress call that shares it.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a retry-decorated function is called re-entrantly (recursion) or concurrently from another thread while an earlier call is still running. Mechanism: the earlier call's self._local.statistics is the same dict object as wrapped_f.statistics, so the new call's clear() empties it mid-run. The original code rebound the attribute to a fresh copy dict, which avoided this and was the protection the existing comment describes. Impact: the outer call's statistics (attempt_number, idle_for, etc.) silently reset or show the inner call's values.

findings.description: Calling stats.clear() on the shared statistics dict lets a concurrent or re-entrant invocation reset the statistics of a call still in progress.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same async retry-decorated coroutine function is awaited concurrently (e.g. asyncio.gather) or re-entrantly while an earlier invocation is still retrying. Mechanism: the earlier invocation's self._local.statistics is the same dict as async_wrapped.statistics, so the later call's clear() empties it while the earlier call still uses it. The previous rebinding gave each call its own dict. Impact: statistics read by the earlier call (attempt number, elapsed time) are silently wrong or reset.
